Home/Growth Lab/Net revenue retention

Revenue / Subscription expansion

Net revenue retention

The recurring revenue retained from a fixed cohort of customers paying at the start of the period, including expansion, contraction, and churn within that cohort while excluding new-customer revenue.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The recurring revenue retained from a fixed cohort of customers paying at the start of the period, including expansion, contraction, and churn within that cohort while excluding new-customer revenue.

%

How we use it

We examine whether existing customer revenue grows enough to offset revenue losses and which cohorts need retention or adoption work.

Transparent calculation(Starting-cohort MRR + cohort expansion MRR - cohort contraction MRR - cohort churned MRR) / starting-cohort MRR * 100
starting cohort mrr50,000
expansion mrr8,000
contraction mrr2,000
churned mrr5,000

(50,000 + 8,000 - 2,000 - 5,000) / 50,000 * 100 = 102% NRR.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Starting customer cohort
  • Plan and customer segment
  • Expansion, contraction, and churn movement

Questions we investigate

  • Which losses offset expansion?
  • Is growth concentrated in a few accounts?
  • Are new accounts leaking into the cohort?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Reconcile cohort revenue movements.
  • Investigate contraction and churn drivers.
  • Prioritize adoption and appropriate expansion.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Finance and customer success leads
Monthly after the recurring-revenue ledger closes.

Required data

  • Starting paying customer cohort
  • Monthly normalized recurring-revenue movements
  • Currency and reactivation policies

Read the measure with context

Zero starting MRR makes the rate undefined. Values above 100% are valid. Exclude new accounts and document reactivation, currency, billing normalization, and cohort rules. Aggregate NRR can hide customer churn or account concentration.
